rows: Prepare detailed reports on audit findings.
Prepare financial documents, reports, or budgets.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements
The detailed audit report is a principal deliverable of an audit or assurance engagement.
Report to management about asset utilization and audit results, and recommend changes in operations and financial activities.
Report information to managers or other personnel.; Advise others on business or operational matters.; Advise others on financial matters.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements
Reporting audit results and recommendations to management communicates the engagement's findings.
Collect and analyze data to detect deficient controls, duplicated effort, extravagance, fraud, or non-compliance with laws, regulations, and management policies.
Collect evidence for legal proceedings.; Investigate legal issues.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements
Collecting and analyzing evidence for control failures, fraud, waste, or noncompliance is substantive assurance work; the legal-investigation DWAs reflect a forensic audit variant.
Inspect account books and accounting systems for efficiency, effectiveness, and use of accepted accounting procedures to record transactions.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements
Inspection of books, systems, and accounting procedures produces an evaluation of recordkeeping effectiveness and conformity.
Supervise auditing of establishments, and determine scope of investigation required.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements
Determining scope and supervising the examination are engagement-lead responsibilities directed at the audit outcome.
Confer with company officials about financial and regulatory matters.
Discuss business strategies, practices, or policies with managers.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements

Within this audit-heavy source cluster, conferring with officials supplies and communicates financial or regulatory context for the engagement, but the wording can also describe general advisory work.
Examine and evaluate financial and information systems, recommending controls to ensure system reliability and data integrity.
Examine financial records or processes.; Advise others on financial matters.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements
Evaluating systems and recommending reliability and data-integrity controls is an information-systems or controls-assurance variant, not ownership of system implementation.
Inspect cash on hand, notes receivable and payable, negotiable securities, and canceled checks to confirm records are accurate.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements
Physical and documentary inspection verifies recorded balances as audit evidence.
Examine records and interview workers to ensure recording of transactions and compliance with laws and regulations.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements
Record examination and worker interviews support conclusions about transaction recording and legal compliance.
Prepare, examine, or analyze accounting records, financial statements, or other financial reports to assess accuracy, completeness, and conformance to reporting and procedural standards.
Examine financial records.; Examine financial records or processes.; Analyze business or financial data.
Maintain accounting records, systems, and financial reports
The statement directly combines preparation, examination, and analysis of accounting records and reports for accurate, complete, standards-conforming reporting.
Analyze financial information.; Prepare financial documents.
Maintain accounting records, systems, and financial reports
Adjusting journal entries correct and complete the accounting record before reporting.
Review accounts for discrepancies and reconcile differences.
Conduct financial or regulatory audits.; Examine financial records.
Maintain accounting records, systems, and financial reports
Reconciliation resolves discrepancies so account balances can be maintained accurately; the audit-related DWA makes assurance use plausible as well.
Establish tables of accounts and assign entries to proper accounts.
Maintain accounting records, systems, and financial reports
Creating the chart of accounts and classifying entries establish the structure of the accounting record.
Examine inventory to verify journal and ledger entries.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements
Examining inventory to verify ledger entries is an evidence-verification procedure rather than routine inventory accounting.
Analyze business operations, trends, costs, revenues, financial commitments, and obligations to project future revenues and expenses or to provide advice.
Provide financial planning, analysis, and decision support
Analysis of operations, trends, costs, revenues, and commitments directly produces forecasts and advice for decisions.
Report to management regarding the finances of establishment.
Report information to managers or other personnel.
Provide financial planning, analysis, and decision support
Reporting establishment finances to management makes financial information usable for internal decisions; generic financial-statement issuance would instead fall under ACC-01.
Develop, implement, modify, and document recordkeeping and accounting systems, making use of current computer technology.
Develop business or financial information systems.
Maintain accounting records, systems, and financial reports

Developing, modifying, and documenting accounting and recordkeeping systems directly expresses administration of the financial-information operation. Reviewer adjudication places this work within the financial-record and reporting outcome rather than a separate canonical task.
Evaluate taxpayer finances to determine tax liability, using knowledge of interest and discount rates, annuities, valuation of stocks and bonds, and amortization valuation of depletable assets.
Determine and document tax liabilities and filings
Evaluation of taxpayer finances and valuation inputs establishes the basis and amount of tax liability.
Examine whether the organization's objectives are reflected in its management activities, and whether employees understand the objectives.
Evaluate effectiveness of personnel policies or practices.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements

Testing whether management activity and employee understanding align with organizational objectives is an operational or performance-audit variant, although its DWA also resembles organizational consulting.
Audit payroll and personnel records to determine unemployment insurance premiums, workers' compensation coverage, liabilities, and compliance with tax laws.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements
The explicit audit of payroll and personnel records produces an assurance and compliance determination; tax and insurance subject matter do not change that responsibility.
Review taxpayer accounts, and conduct audits on-site, by correspondence, or by summoning taxpayer to office.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements

Authority-side examination of taxpayer accounts is assigned to audit and assurance because the stated occupational outcome is an audit finding; tax subject matter remains a structured secondary link to ACC-04.
Compute taxes owed and prepare tax returns, ensuring compliance with payment, reporting, or other tax requirements.
Calculate tax information.; Prepare financial documents, reports, or budgets.
Determine and document tax liabilities and filings
Computing tax owed and preparing a compliant return directly expresses the tax-accounting outcome.
Advise clients in areas such as compensation, employee health care benefits, the design of accounting or data processing systems, or long-range tax or estate plans.
Advise others on human resources topics.
Provide financial planning, analysis, and decision support

The statement's common outcome is client advice for long-range organizational or financial choices, but it combines compensation, benefits, systems, tax, and estate domains that cannot be split under one-to-one mapping.
Direct activities of personnel engaged in filing, recording, compiling, and transmitting financial records.
Maintain accounting records, systems, and financial reports

Directing staff who file, record, compile, and transmit financial records administers the recordkeeping operation; it may also evidence a broader formal-management responsibility not otherwise represented. Reviewer adjudication places this work within the financial-record and reporting outcome rather than a separate canonical task.
Conduct pre-implementation audits to determine if systems and programs under development will work as planned.
Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements
A pre-implementation audit evaluates whether a system or program will operate as planned, a prospective systems-assurance setting.
